Intro: Not bad for what you've got.
I respect your resourcefulness. You make do with what you have, and it's almost quality.
Restaurants like yours are expendable. We will no longer need your service.
This establishment will be closed, and you will be—
…Baklava? You should not have given me this.
Baklava… it is indulgent. In a way, an antithesis of everything I've built. Sticky, sweet, messy—encased in a fragile shell built to be broken.
I spent decades in pharmacology. I executed every procedure and experiment with pinpoint accuracy.
My work is, and always has been, of logic and precision. That is how I rule Verehn.
I do not cave to pleasure, that sweet, oily sheen that coats your tongue.
The Moshchny—they fed themselves and their people on frivolous indulgence and sugar, making them fat and lazy with content.
This was made to be flaky, dripping. It's supposed to coat your fingers in a sticky sweet film, to be licked off with a smile.
Like an opium for the masses. Obsessive, addictive, and easy. Reminds those who eat of it of a softer, kinder time.
Sustenance is the cornerstone of our civilization, and indulgence of it, our culture. This baklava…
